h1_main: Best Helicopter Tours in Budapest in 2026
author_role: 5 scenic flights compared on price per seat, price per minute, take-off point and route
lead: The right scenic flight is the one that fits your group: a private helicopter over the Parliament for 2 or 3, a group of 4 with the transfer handled, the Danube Bend from the air, or an open-air flight on a smaller budget. This page gets you to that seat in under a minute.

To make the choice easy, I compared all 5 on what really decides it: price per seat (helicopters are priced per aircraft), price per minute in the air, take-off point, transfer and route, checked on each seller's own page. Filter by helicopter, under €200 a seat, transfer, Danube Bend or open-air below, or scroll straight to the ranking.

review: This is the cheapest way into a helicopter over Budapest: €550 for a private 20-minute flight for up to 3 passengers. Fill all three seats and it is €183.33 each, or €27.50 per minute of flight time for the aircraft, roughly half the per-minute rate of the 15-minute flight at #2.

The route is a proper city loop rather than a quick hop: up over Gellért Hill and the Citadel, along the Danube past the Chain Bridge and Liberty Bridge, over the Royal Palace and the Parliament, then out over Margaret Island and János Hill, Budapest's highest point, with the Erzsébet Lookout Tower. You check in at Budaörs Airport (LHBS), and the itinerary includes an optional 5-minute photo stop.

The trade-offs are logistics and size. No transfer is listed, so budget a taxi to Kőérberki út 36/A, and the aircraft takes 3 passengers, so a group of 4 should look at #2 or #3. Flights depend on the weather, and a weather cancellation gets a full refund.

review: Heli Hungary's flight is the one to book if the Danube Bend is on your list. For €980 for up to 4 passengers (€245 each when full) you choose between a Budapest sightseeing route and a flight north over Visegrád and the Danube Bend, the only helicopter listing here that names Visegrád.

It is booked as a 1-hour slot, and the time actually airborne within that hour is not broken down, so you cannot compare it minute for minute with #1 and #2. What you can compare is the experience around it: a turbine helicopter, a pilot who gives commentary along the way, an audio guide, and the option of a sunset flight. It is also the only flight here listed as wheelchair-accessible.

Take-off is from the same Kőérberki út address as #1, by Budaörs Airport, and no transfer is listed. It has the longest track record of the helicopter options, with a perfect score across a dozen-plus reviews. If the Danube Bend appeals but a helicopter does not fit the budget, a Danube Bend day trip covers Visegrád on the ground for a fraction of the price.

review: A gyrocopter is the budget way to fly over Budapest, and arguably the more thrilling one. From €149 per person you sit in an open or closed cockpit next to a licensed pilot, and on the open version there is no window between you and the view.

The three routes are the reason to look at it. Above Budapest (25–30 min) loops over the Parliament, Chain Bridge and Danube; Hundred Lakes (35–45 min) follows South Budapest's lake system; Danube Bend (60–75 min) is the long one, out over Margaret Island and up to the Bend. The listing does not say which route the €149 from-price covers; if it is the city loop, that works out at €5–6 a minute, against €27.50 for the cheapest helicopter.

Two catches. The airfield is Farkashegy in Budakeszi, just outside the city, and no transfer is listed. And the rating is mixed so far, at 3.7 across only a handful of reviews. It suits adventurous travellers flying on their own; because it is priced per person, a full helicopter gets closer in price per seat as your group grows.

The 10-minute flight works out at about €11 a minute; the 30-minute flight costs more, so compare both options when you book if you want longer air time. Watch the limits: over-12s only and a 91 kg maximum. It is a new listing, so there are no reviews yet.

guide.h2: Budapest Scenic Flights Side by Side
guide.html:
The helicopters are sold per group, the gyrocopter and hang-glider per person. To compare them fairly, look at price per seat when the aircraft is full and price per minute in the air.

Reading the table: for 3 people, #1 is the clear value pick. For 4, #2 costs only €14 more per seat than a full #1 and includes the transfer, but gives 5 fewer minutes. Solo, a helicopter seat costs €550–980, so the gyrocopter and hang-glider are the realistic options.

• Couple or group of 3, best value: #1 Aeroglobe, 20 minutes for €550.
  • Family or group of 4: #2 Balaton Fly (transfer and sparkling wine included) or #3 Heli Hungary for a longer slot.
  • You want the Danube Bend: #3 Heli Hungary by helicopter, or #4 gyrocopter's 60–75 minute route on your own.
  • Special occasion: #2 for the fizz, or #3 with a sunset flight on request.
  • Solo and adventurous: #4 gyrocopter for open-cockpit thrills, #5 hang-glider for the lowest price and a take-off inside the city.
  • Wheelchair user: #3 is the only flight listed as wheelchair-accessible.

guide.h2: Where the Flights Take Off (and How to Get There)
guide.html:
No flight leaves from the riverbank. Plan the journey before you book:

  • Budaörs Airport (LHBS), Kőérberki út 36/A: #1 and #3. On the south-western edge of Budapest; no transfer, so take a taxi or drive.
  • Heliport via Batthyány tér: #2. The return transfer is included, so this is the easiest from a central hotel.
  • Farkashegy Airfield, Budakeszi: #4. In the hills west of Buda, outside the city limits; no transfer.
  • Hármashatárhegy, Cenk utca 3 (District II): #5. Inside the city on the Buda hills; transport from the base of the hill to the airfield is included.

guide.h2: Weather, Limits and What to Bring
guide.html:
Weather: all flights depend on it. Aeroglobe (#1) states that a weather cancellation gets a full refund, and all five come with free cancellation up to 24 hours before, so book for the start of your trip and keep a spare day to rebook. The gyrocopter flies year-round.

Weight and age limits: the hang-glider takes passengers aged 12+ up to 91 kg; the gyrocopter up to 118 kg. The gyrocopter is not for people afraid of heights or with vertigo, and #1 is not suitable for people with vertigo either. On #2, children get noise-cancelling earplugs.

What to bring: sunglasses, a camera and comfortable clothes (#1). Drones are not allowed on #1, loose clothing is not allowed on the gyrocopter, and alcohol is not allowed before the hang-glider flight.

Time to allow: #2's 15 minutes in the air is a 1.5–2 hour outing with the transfer and safety briefing. For #1, #3 and #4, add your own travel time to Budaörs or Budakeszi.

Cheaper ways to see the same sights: the Parliament and the bridges look spectacular from the water too: compare the best Budapest river cruises or, for a private occasion, private boat tours. Planning the rest of your days? See the best things to do in Budapest.

faqs.q: How much is a helicopter tour in Budapest?
faqs.a: From €550 per group (up to 3 passengers, 20 minutes) to €980 (up to 4 passengers, 1-hour slot). Full, that is €183–245 a seat. A 15-minute flight for up to 4 with transfer costs €790.

faqs.q: Is a Budapest helicopter tour priced per person?
faqs.a: No. All three helicopter flights here are priced per group: up to 3 passengers on #1 and up to 4 on #2 and #3. The gyrocopter (€149) and powered hang-glider (€109.79) are per person.

faqs.q: Where do helicopter tours in Budapest take off?
faqs.a: #1 and #3 fly from Budaörs Airport on the city's south-western edge (Kőérberki út 36/A). #2 includes a transfer from Batthyány tér to the heliport. The gyrocopter flies from Farkashegy in Budakeszi, the hang-glider from Hármashatárhegy in District II.

faqs.q: Can I fly over the Danube Bend from Budapest?
faqs.a: Yes. Heli Hungary's 1-hour helicopter flight offers a Visegrád and Danube Bend route for up to 4, and the gyrocopter has a 60–75 minute Danube Bend route, priced per person.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest scenic flight in Budapest?
faqs.a: The powered hang-glider at €109.79 for 10 minutes, taking off from Hármashatárhegy inside the city. The gyrocopter starts at €149 per person, with routes from 25–30 minutes.

faqs.q: What will I see on a Budapest helicopter flight?
faqs.a: The city routes cover the Parliament, Buda Castle and the Royal Palace, the Chain Bridge and Elizabeth Bridge, Gellért Hill with the Citadel, Margaret Island and, depending on the flight, St Stephen's Basilica, Heroes' Square or the Buda Hills. Read up on the Parliament before you fly over it.

methodology: We compared 5 scenic flights over Budapest, three helicopters, a gyrocopter and a powered hang-glider, side by side on price per seat when full, price per minute in the air, maximum passengers, take-off point, transfers, route and passenger limits. Prices are live from-prices for a standard date in November 2026.
